goal: Declare docs/reference/host-capability.md, rendered by scripts/render-host-capability.ts, as a derived output in docs/agents/derived-files.json so batch integration regenerates the capability table instead of parking two Lanes that both change capability rows with batch_integration_conflict "conflicts include undeclared outputs" (batch #481, S8 vs S5). Out of scope: the render script, the capability declarations and table content, and batch-start declaration_head semantics. no user-visible change: this edits repository tooling metadata and its test; the rendered reference document is unchanged.

acceptance.assertion: docs/agents/derived-files.json, read through the strict readDerivedFiles reader, has exactly one entry whose outputs include HOST_CAPABILITY_PATH exported by scripts/render-host-capability.ts (docs/reference/host-capability.md); that entry's outputs are exactly that path, its generate is bun scripts/render-host-capability.ts, its check is bun scripts/render-host-capability.ts --check, and its sources include scripts/render-host-capability.ts, plugins/immune-brain/runtime/host-core/capability.ts, plugins/immune-brain/runtime/claude/capability.ts, plugins/immune-brain/runtime/antigravity/capability.ts and plugins/immune-brain/.pi-extension/pi-capability.ts. Running the declared check argv from the repository root exits 0 on the current tree. The extended test in tests/derived-files.test.ts (next to the existing repository Claude bundle declaration test) fails when the entry is missing, when the output path differs from HOST_CAPABILITY_PATH, or when a listed source is dropped. The existing Claude and Antigravity package derived-files tests stay green. Done looks like: a maintainer reads one host-capability-reference entry in the registry and the repository derived-files test passes.
